pr_title: sql/catalog: avoid cached lease descriptors for validation
pr_body:
Fixes: #79396

Previously, to optimize validation we would use leased
descriptors from inside the collection for validation.
This could be problematic since there are cases where
stale descriptors may be leased, for example for OID
looks up during the bind, which can cause incorrect
validation errors if any dependent objects are looked
up. To address this, this patch removes the optimization
that prefers the use of cached leased descriptors and instead
goes through the normal look-up logic.

Release note: None

Jira issue: CRDB-14800
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/79397)

*[pkg/sql/catalog/descs/validate.go, line 97 at r1](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/79397#-MzrZ10_D8kSxmDoZoLh:-MzrZ10_D8kSxmDoZoLi:b-6g0wlu) ([raw file](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/400483956bbc9fe439ba95113ccc577d20627698/pkg/sql/catalog/descs/validate.go#L97)):*
> ```Go
> 		}
> 		if uc, _ := c.tc.uncommitted.getImmutableByID(desc.GetID()); uc == nil {
> 			desc, err = c.tc.uncommitted.add(desc.NewBuilder().BuildExistingMutable(), notValidatedYet)
> ```

curious what's the benefit of caching newly read descriptors into the uncommitted layer since we're not trying to update these descriptors anyway right?


<!-- Sent from Reviewable.io -->

> curious what's the benefit of caching newly read descriptors into the uncommitted layer since we're not trying to update these descriptors anyway right?

We might want to mutate them later on in the transaction. Really the caching should be in the `kvDescriptors` layer but that would imply that and the uncommitted layer would need to talk to each other, because mutating a descriptor would have to invalidate the corresponding kv cache entry.

I should have caught this at the time. We can't use the cache to validate descriptors because it doesn't provide a consistent snapshot, and our validation logic wasn't written to take version skew into consideration. In principle, when we are modifying a descriptor, most of the time or all of the time, we should already have read its cross references, so we shouldn't need to be paying twice.
I can't even remember why or how we thought it would be OK to do this, to be honest.

issue_context.title: sql/catalog: stale leased descriptors can lead to validation errors
issue_context.body:
**Describe the problem**

Please describe the issue you observed, and any steps we can take to reproduce it:

When running the randomized schema changer workload we found that the validation logic
can intermittently fail if the transaction looked up a leased descriptor earlier. For example,
when binding OIDs we may use an older version of a leased descriptor, versus the
one we should be validating against. When the validation logic kicks in it can then use 
the incorrect version of the descriptor for dependent objects, which can lead
to validation errors.

**To Reproduce**

The easiest reproduction is to run schemachanger/random-load concurrently 8 ways and the reproduction can be hit in < 5 minutes. Normally involving a view backreference not being found in a table descriptor.
